messages:
Alex: Heads-up, seeing a ~8% GPU capacity drop in us-west2 and ECC error rate jumped 6x over the last 10m. Some pods are retrying and autoscale is pending.
Cheng: Link to the dashboard? Is this across multiple racks or one zone?
Alex: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/cluster/gpu-health?orgId=1&var-region=us-west2
Alex: quick log snippet from node gpu-rack7-node11:\n```
[2026-03-18T17:02:12Z] nvml: ECC error count increased: device 2 -> 137 (+12)
[2026-03-18T17:03:05Z] kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, submission timeout
[2026-03-18T17:04:01Z] kubelet: pod mymodel-abc crashed with GPU allocation failure
```
Oncall-Bot: alert: GPU-ECC-SPIKE detected in us-west2 (severity: high). Incident created INT-2026-4421.
Maria: Ok, triage plan: (1) isolate affected nodes so we don't cause cluster-wide drains, (2) route high-QPS customer workloads to us-central temporarily, (3) mark faulty GPUs for replacement and schedule vendor RMA for the rack.
Tiago: Can someone run `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` and `kubectl describe node gpu-rack7-node11`? Also post the output of `lsmod | grep nvidia` (driver version).
Alex: pasted outputs: `nvidia-driver 515.76` and ECC report shows multiple corrected and some uncorrected counts. Xid codes seen: 13, 31, 43.\n
Jamie: Sounds like flakey memory on a subset of cards, not a software regression. But we did push a driver micro-update last week — worth double-checking boards that got the update. If confirmed hardware, RMA. In the meantime, reduce memory pressure: enable model-fallback to smaller instance types for non-SLA traffic and lower batch sizes on heavy routes.
Infra-Bot: 4 nodes in us-west2 marked Unhealthy by heathcheck. Auto-provisioner spun 2 replacements (pending). Estimated spin-up: 7m.
Cheng: Operations checklist: 1) cordon + drain gpu-rack7-node11..node14 (use --ignore-daemonsets) 2) tag GPUs as RMA in inventory 3) open vswitch route for canary traffic to us-central 4) create postmortem JIRA and link to INT-2026-4421.
Maria: Cost note: rerouting to us-central will increase egress and on-demand spend. Rough back-of-envelope: if we shift 250 qps sustained, expect ~$6k/day extra for the baseline replication and preemptible replacements. Put a cost cap on the incident response if needed.
Tiago: I'm starting the drains now. Command I'm running:\n```
kubectl cordon gpu-rack7-node11 && kubectl drain gpu-rack7-node11 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=120
```
Will proceed node-by-node.
Alex: Routing change done: updated smart-router policy to de-prioritize us-west2 for internal-high and customer-critical routes. After 4m error rate dropped from 6x -> 2x. Capacity still -4% until replacements finish.
Jamie: Keep an eye on Xid 31 frequency after the first replacement. If it persists across multiple cards, escalate to vendor for firmware/hw trace. Also coordinate with sales for any affected customers.
Oncall-Bot: Incident INT-2026-4421 updated: mitigations in place, replacements scheduled, next update in 30m.
Alex: I'll capture failed GPU IDs and attach to the JIRA. Thanks all. :raised_hands:\n
